message.content:
For a reflection through a plane with unit normal vector \(\mathbf n\), the reflection matrix is  
\[
R=I-2\mathbf n\mathbf n^T.
\]
Thus the normal vector is an eigenvector of \(R\) with eigenvalue \(-1\). So we solve
\[
(R+I)\mathbf n=0.
\]

The given matrix is
\[
R=\begin{pmatrix}
\frac{11}{15}&\frac{2}{15}&\frac{2}{3}\\
\frac{2}{15}&\frac{14}{15}&-\frac{1}{3}\\
\frac{2}{3}&-\frac{1}{3}&-\frac{2}{3}
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then
\[
R+I=
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac{26}{15}&\frac{2}{15}&\frac{2}{3}\\
\frac{2}{15}&\frac{29}{15}&-\frac{1}{3}\\
\frac{2}{3}&-\frac{1}{3}&\frac{1}{3}
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Multiplying by \(15\), we solve
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
26&2&10\\
2&29&-5\\
10&-5&5
\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{pmatrix}=0.
\]
This gives
\[
13x+y+5z=0,
\]
\[
2x+29y-5z=0,
\]
\[
2x-y+z=0.
\]
From the last equation,
\[
z=y-2x.
\]
Substitute into the first:
\[
13x+y+5(y-2x)=0
\]
\[
3x+6y=0
\]
\[
x=-2y.
\]
Then
\[
z=y-2(-2y)=5y.
\]
So a normal vector is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}-2\\1\\5\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Choosing the opposite sign so that \(a>0\), we get
\[
\begin{pmatrix}2\\-1\\-5\end{pmatrix}.
\]

The answer is \(\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ -5 \end{pmatrix}\).
